clue.text: Agree with conscientious objector in prison, say

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the phrase is spoken rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: someone in prison is said to be inside

explanation.surface: Someone agrees alongside a jailed conscientious objector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that INSIDE (in prison) is pronounced, written INCIDE to follow CO.
explanation.definitionFit: To coincide is to correspond or be in accord, a synonym of agree.

clue.text: Stone is no end of a snob

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter is taken away from the word for snob

parts.note: snob is an old word for a cobbler or shoemaker

explanation.definitionFit: A cobble is a rounded paving stone.

clue.text: Annoyed girl, having tried awkwardly to embrace her

indicators.note: to embrace means one piece is held inside the other
awkwardly tells us to rearrange the letters of tried

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is annoyed when someone clumsily tries to hug her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' turns TRIED into IRTED, which 'to embrace' wraps round RITA: IR-RITA-TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated is a synonym of annoyed or vexed.

clue.text: Moulding outside cover round a of bone

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Moulding outside cover round a of bone'; the scan smudges the word before 'of bone' (ends in d), so the piece giving T cannot be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Moulding outside cover round a of bone

clue.text: Daniel is fed up with Old English

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word fed is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Daniel has had enough of Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English novelist who wrote Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Seating for choir in All Saints, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the word All inside the abbreviation for Saints

parts.note: Sts is the abbreviation for Saints, as in Sts Peter and Paul
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choir seating in a church called All Saints.
explanation.definitionFit: Choir stalls are the rows of seats in a church chancel where the singers sit.

clue.text: Seine fisherman going to sea?

parts.note: a seine is a fishing net, not the Paris river, so this is a fishing vessel heading out

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that tows a large net through the sea to catch fish is the boat described.

clue.text: Franz lost note from Rachel on: the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue the way up means the remaining letters are read from bottom to top
lost means the note is dropped from the name Rachel

parts.note: C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Franz misplaced a memo from Rachel as he climbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes C from RACHEL to leave RAHEL, which 'the way up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian composer of the operetta The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Proof of spirit power.

definitions.meaning: the alcoholic content of a drink, measured as proof

explanation.definitionFit: A drink's alcohol content is called its proof or potency, and the same word means might.

clue.text: Will. 'this ball, transposed, terminate one's innings?

indicators.note: transposed means the two halves of the phrase change places

parts.note: to break off is to terminate or end

explanation.surface: A bowler wonders whether this delivery will end the batsman's innings.
explanation.walkthrough: An off break is a cricket delivery that turns from the off side; it might well end a batsman's innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An off break is a type of spinning delivery bowled in cricket, a ball.

clue.text: Proverbially they act sheepishly

parts.note: the proverb says like-minded creatures flock together, and flocking is acting like sheep

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says birds of this kind flock together, which is what sheep do, so the clue describes people who stick with their own kind.

clue.text: She's a Latvian with diamonds!

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A Latvian woman dripping with diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettice is a woman's name, so it fits the pronoun she.

clue.text: Type of 23 straight from the battle

parts.note: the bull terrier is a breed of terrier, the answer at 23
a straight is a run, as of cards or a racecourse straight

explanation.surface: A breed of dog coming straight out of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: First Bull Run was an American Civil War battle (1861).
explanation.definitionFit: Bull Run is the name of a battle of the American Civil War, fought twice near Manassas.

clue.text: Keep still, by the way, and relatively close

parts.note: St, short for street, is a way
agnate means related through the male line, close as a relative

explanation.surface: Someone told to stay put, as a near relation, along the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to remain motionless and inactive, not flowing or moving.

clue.text: Despotism is, to the French, a sort of one-off charity.

parts.note: au is French for to the

indicators.note: a sort of signals a rearrangement of the word charity once the single letter is taken out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tyranny described by a Frenchman as a peculiar unique act of giving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-off' asks for I (one) to be removed from CHARITY; 'a sort of' rearranges CHARTY into TARCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Autarchy means absolute rule by one person, a synonym of despotism.

clue.text: About suitable for dockyard job

parts.note: re means about or concerning
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Something suitable for work in a dockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is the overhaul and re-equipping of a ship, done in a dockyard.

clue.text: Blow-pipe instrumental in getting something for the pot

definitions.meaning: a small wind instrument of the recorder family
a kind of kidney bean cooked as a vegetable

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small end-blown flute and a pale green French bean used in cooking.

clue.text: Animal which lays eggs by water supply at random

definitions.text: Animal which lays eggs by water

indicators.note: random tells us the letters of supply and at are shuffled

explanation.surface: An egg-laying creature living by a randomly supplied stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is 'random'; 'at' is part of the fodder, not of 'at random'.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed Australian mammal is one of the few that lay eggs, and it lives along rivers.

clue.text: What metal-detectors want to find in abundance, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is identified by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: loads means plenty or an abundance

explanation.surface: Treasure hunters hope to find plenty of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodes are veins of metal ore in rock, the deposits a prospector hopes to find.

clue.text: Expertise applicable to fiction-writing

definitions.meaning: skill or knowledge, as in the arts and the ... of a trade
the word that comes before fiction to name the genre of space and future stories

explanation.definitionFit: A systematic body of skill is one sense, and the genre of futuristic stories is named with this word before fiction.

clue.text: Detract from Chinese restaurant?

definitions.meaning: to subtract or remove, as in it takes away from his achievement
a shop selling cooked food to eat elsewhere, Chinese being a typical example

explanation.definitionFit: To lessen something is to take from it, and a shop selling meals to carry off is the British name for such an eatery.

clue.text: Letters make it clear to apprentice

definitions.meaning: the word the, a few letters, makes a noun definite
to bind someone as a trainee clerk

explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's definite one makes a noun specific, and to bind a trainee by contract is the verb sense.

clue.text: Call on Tunisian leader to have notes complied with

parts.note: O is a call, as in O come all ye faithful
the Bey was the ruler of Tunis under the Ottomans
E and D are two musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone calls on the ruler of Tunisia to get his memos obeyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bey was the title of the ruler of Tunis.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeyed means did as instructed, the same as complied with.

clue.text: Man-at-arms of Scottish breed, maybe

definitions.meaning: a member of the British Territorial Army, a part-time soldier
Scottish, Skye and Cairn are breeds of small dog of this kind

explanation.definitionFit: A Territorial Army volunteer soldier is nicknamed this, and it is also a type of dog including the Scottish breed.

clue.text: Country has' right' to: mountain range

parts.note: the Urals are the mountain range dividing Europe from Asia

explanation.surface: A nation claims rights to a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective, as in country life, means belonging to the countryside.

clue.text: Basil dropped in as a matter of good taste

definitions.text: Basil dropped in as a matter of good taste

parts.words: Basil dropped in as a matter of good taste
parts.note: a leaf such as basil is dropped into the cooking vessel to give flavour, good taste here meaning flavour, not refinement

explanation.surface: Basil turned up out of politeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A culinary plant used to flavour stews and soups, such as basil, is a pot-herb.

clue.text: Connected with Cupid

parts.note: a chubby winged boy in Renaissance art, a figure of the Roman god of love

explanation.definitionFit: A putto is a cherub-like infant in art, the figure that represents the god of love.

clue.text: Painter they call crazy (like this)

indicators.note: crazy tells us to jumble the letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: An artist is called mad by others.
explanation.walkthrough: '(like this)' is the definition: a phrase in brackets is put in parenthetically.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark set in brackets is inserted as an aside, and that is the manner of the bracketed words here.

clue.text: Sea cook's side of beef

parts.note: Long John, the ship's cook in Treasure Island, has a surname that with side added names a cut of beef

explanation.definitionFit: Long John of Treasure Island was a sea cook, and silverside is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter.

clue.text: Interfered with spy' having key to break signal code

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: to break means the letter for the key splits the code letters open

parts.note: STD, subscriber trunk dialling, is the old British telephone dialling code
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A spy with a key cracks a signal code and meddles.
explanation.walkthrough: STD code was the British term for a long-distance dialling code.
explanation.definitionFit: Molested once meant simply bothered or meddled with, a sense close to interfered with.
